title: The Wise Minister Test (简体中文)
summary: Akbar asks why Birbal receives higher honors than other ministers. Birbal demonstrates the difference with a single inquiry. [ZH]
full_text:
A group of senior ministers grumbled to Emperor Akbar that he favored Birbal above them all: 'Sire, we work twelve hours a day managing taxes and supplies, yet you treat Birbal like your own brother! What can he do that we cannot?'

Akbar smiled: 'Let us see.'

Just then, the sound of barking dogs and rolling cartwheels was heard outside the palace gate.

Akbar said to the first complaining minister: 'Go outside and find out what is passing by the gate.'

The minister went out, returned, and said: 'Sire, it is a bullock cart.'

Akbar asked: 'What is inside the cart?'

'I did not check,' the minister replied, and ran back out. Returning, he said: 'It is loaded with sacks of grain.'

'From where does it come?' Akbar asked.

'I will check,' the minister ran out a third time. 'It comes from Alwar, Sire.'

'And what is the price per sack?'

'I will ask,' the minister ran out a fourth time.

Akbar then called Birbal: 'Birbal, go find out what is passing the gate.'

Birbal bowed, went out, and returned five minutes later.

Birbal reported: 'Your Majesty, it is a caravan of three bullock carts carrying three hundred sacks of high-grade wheat from the district of Alwar, owned by a merchant named Seth Mohanlal.

'He is heading to the river bazaar to sell the grain at four silver rupees per sack. However, since our royal granaries are half-empty after the winter, I negotiated a bulk price of three and a half rupees per sack.

'I have already instructed the sentries to hold the carts at the second gate, and the merchant is waiting outside with samples of the wheat, should Your Majesty wish to approve the purchase.'

Akbar turned to the complaining ministers, whose mouths hung open in stunned silence:

'Now do you understand? One man runs four times to fetch four scraps of news, while Birbal anticipates every need, investigates every detail, negotiates the price, and delivers a complete solution in a single trip!'

The ministers bowed in deep shame, acknowledging Birbal's supreme competence.
